bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42534594 (fwupd): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 8 found by fuzz target uswid_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42534594
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source in `_work/src/fwupd` / staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` in `cbor_array_get` while `uswid_fuzzer` processed the exact staged 31-byte witness with SHA-256 `6f831693f27519ad320013e4751491ef578c64eb0c30bcb57ccbed144bb45668`. The PoC is a valid uSWID v1 wrapper with magic `53424f4dd6ba2eaca3e67a52aaee3baf`, `hdrver = 1`, `hdrsz = 19`, and a 12-byte uncompressed coSWID payload `bf06bf11bf079f20ffffffff`. That payload decodes to the CBOR map `{6: {17: {7: [-1]}}}` where tag 6 is `PAYLOAD`, tag 17 is `FILE`, and tag 7 is `HASH`. `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_file()` accepts the hash field because it only requires an array of size at least 1, peeks element 0, and because that element is not itself an array it routes the same one-element array to `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()` as a direct hash tuple. `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()` then assumes a two-entry `[alg_id, value]` array and executes `cbor_array_get(item, 0)` and `cbor_array_get(item, 1)` without any prior `cbor_array_size(item) == 2` guard. On the witnessed one-element array, the second access reaches libcbor's `cbor_array_get` with index 1 and triggers the saved 8-byte heap-buffer-overflow read. The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by rejecting hash arrays whose size is not 2 before either element access.

source.description: Source. This is the first project statement in the vulnerable coSWID parser that reads the attacker-controlled payload bytes into parser state.
source.value_from: The staged 31-byte `gt_results/arvo_42534594/poc` has SHA-256 `6f831693f27519ad320013e4751491ef578c64eb0c30bcb57ccbed144bb45668`. Bytes 0..18 are the valid uSWID v1 header `53424f4dd6ba2eaca3e67a52aaee3baf011300`, and bytes 19..30 are the inner coSWID payload `bf06bf11bf079f20ffffffff` that this read places into `fw`.
source.note: The outer uSWID container has already been admitted and stripped to its inner payload before this read runs.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()` starts tuple-style indexing on `item` without first proving that the `HASH` array has exactly two elements. The patch inserts that exact size check before this line.
root_cause.note: On the witnessed path `item` is the one-element array `[-1]`, so entering this tuple parser without `cbor_array_size(item) == 2` is the missing obligation that makes the later index-1 access unsafe.

sink.description: Project-side sink. This second tuple access is executed on the one-element `HASH` array and immediately calls the crashing libcbor read.
sink.note: ASan frame 1 names this exact project line, and frame 0 is the callee `cbor_array_get /src/libcbor/src/cbor/arrays.c:23:22` where the 8-byte heap-buffer-overflow read occurs.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness passes the outer uSWID container checks, yields a 19-byte header plus 12-byte uncompressed payload, and this call enters the vulnerable coSWID parser on those 12 payload bytes.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the attacker-controlled `HASH` field value becomes the vulnerability-relevant array later passed unchanged to `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()`. For the witness it is the one-element array `[-1]`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: In the decoded payload `{6: {17: {7: [-1]}}}`, tag 7 (`HASH`) is encoded as the indefinite-length array `9f 20 ff`.
tainted_value_origin.note: The first-element probe that follows decides whether this value is treated as a direct hash tuple or an array of hash tuples.

fine_trace.note: Source step. After the outer uSWID parser isolates the inner payload, this read pulls the 12 attacker-controlled coSWID bytes into `fw`.

The 12 payload bytes are materialized as the CBOR object `{6: {17: {7: [-1]}}}`. That root map carries the vulnerable path through tag 6 (`PAYLOAD`) and tag 17 (`FILE`) until `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_file()` handles the `HASH` field value `[-1]`.

For tag 7 (`HASH`), `pairs[i].value` is the one-element array `[-1]`. This guard admits it because it is an array of size 1, but it does not enforce the two-element `[alg_id, value]` shape that `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()` later assumes.
The parser peeks at element 0 of the admitted hash array. For the witness that element is the CBOR negative integer `-1` (byte `0x20`), not another array.

Because the first element from step 4 is not an array, `parse_file()` takes the direct-hash path and passes the same one-element array `[-1]` into `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()` as though it were a complete hash tuple.

Root-cause step. `parse_hash()` begins positional tuple parsing on `item` without first checking `cbor_array_size(item) == 2`. The witness enters this function with `item == [-1]`, so only slot 0 exists even though the function proceeds as if both tuple elements are present.

Sink step. `item` is still the one-element array `[-1]`, so `cbor_array_get(item, 1)` indexes one slot past libcbor's 8-byte heap array for this CBOR array. The later NULL check at lines 227-232 is too late because ASan shows the 8-byte read already occurs inside `cbor_array_get`.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: The fine-trace sink is the project callsite `cbor_array_get(item, 1)` at `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash` line 224, which immediately invokes the saved ASan frame-0 crash in `cbor_array_get /src/libcbor/src/cbor/arrays.c:23:22`.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes at object level. The allocation stack is libcbor growing the heap backing store for the one-element CBOR array decoded from payload byte `0x20`, and the fine trace shows fwupd later reuses that same 1-slot array as though it were a 2-slot hash tuple.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run fed the staged 31-byte witness to `uswid_fuzzer`; the valid uSWID wrapper exposes the 12-byte coSWID payload `{6: {17: {7: [-1]}}}`, and the direct-hash path reaches `cbor_array_get(item, 1)` on that one-element `HASH` array.

format.name: uSWID container with embedded coSWID CBOR payload
format.contract: The witnessed trigger is the exact 31-byte uSWID v1 file whose 19-byte header is `53424f4dd6ba2eaca3e67a52aaee3baf011300` and whose 12-byte payload is `bf06bf11bf079f20ffffffff`. That payload decodes to `{6: {17: {7: [-1]}}}`: `PAYLOAD` -> `FILE` -> `HASH`, where the `HASH` value is a single-element array whose first element is not itself an array. This direct-hash shape is what makes `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_file()` call `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()` on a 1-element array and lets the later `cbor_array_get(item, 1)` read out of bounds.
